ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The picture is a life cycle diagram of an earwig (earwig); on the left there is a small cluster of oval eggs, and a black arrow points from these eggs to the smaller, immature earwig form above; at the lower right there is also a larger adult form, and the whole process is connected with arrows. Reasoning: The question asks “which life cycle stage comes after the egg.” According to the arrow starting from the eggs in the picture, after the eggs hatch, they enter the smaller immature earwig stage. Biologically, the juvenile stage of this kind of insect with incomplete metamorphosis is called nymph (nymph).
